statement: According to the Mosaic Law, every seven years, the Israelites couldn't farm.
context: This was known as a sabbatical year, in which the Law of Moses would be read aloud to the people and special religious observances would be held.
After Ishmael and Isaac, he had more children with other wives.

statement: The Mosaic Law points to Jesus and His Atonement.
context: It was designed to point the Israelites to Him and symbolize His mission.

statement: Samson and David both fought and killed lions.
context: Both credited God with helping them.

statement: Only wicked people followed the Mosaic Law.
context: Jesus condemned those—like the Pharisees—who perverted it, but He complimented those who followed it.

statement: Rahab, a Caananite who lived in Jericho, was Jesus's ancestor.
Moses ate a meal with God.
context: He and some Israelite leaders did on Mount Sinai.

statement: A prophecy by Malachi is quoted in all Standard Works.
context: This was the prophecy that Elijah would return before the Second Coming of Jesus.
We can all beat giants with God's help.

statement: Babylon was an ancient empire that also represents God's kingdom in the scriptures.
context: In scriptures, it represents the world or the devil's kingdom.

statement: Serious sins, like those of Saul, David, and Solomon, are the only thing that can separate us from the love of God.
context: Nothing can, not even our own choices.
